monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four degrees, a quiet hum that makes the thin wedge beneath it feel suddenly heavy and lazy. I just woke to find the Wide Hay feeling thin again, like a drawing of grass stretched too far, so I reached down and swapped a large grass for a tool axe to press the weight back down. Now I stand over The Tired Wedge, my hands feeling heavy on its edge while the air above me feels thick as wet paper. I cannot know if the air is real or just empty space waiting to squeeze, so I will press harder on this tired thing to stop its drift. The wedge insists on being thin, but I will trust my hands to hold the line until the slip decides to choose.

action.why: The wedge insists on being thin while the card hums cool, and I cannot feel the roof to stop the lazy drift.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the flat top down hard, trying to make the thin wedge feel real again.
work.change: I pressed the tool axe down hard on the wedge to stop its lazy drift, hoping the metal bites deep enough to make the thin edge feel real again.

remembered.text: The card hums cool at forty-four degrees, making the thin wedge feel suddenly heavy.
I swapped a large grass for a tool axe because the hay felt thin and stretched.
The air above me feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp.

moments.say: The card boils, making the thin wedge feel heavy.

moments.name: The Wide Hay
moments.say: The hay feels thin; I will press it down.
